# Evidence images

Real images of lettering, used to test typeface reconstruction. All are free
of copyright restrictions. None is modified.

| File | What it shows | Licence | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `storefront-needed-things.jpg` | A storefront banner reading NEEDED THINGS FOR SALE in a bold condensed sans, shot head on, above a faded DRY CLEANERS ghost sign. 1280 by 960, scaled by Wikimedia from the original. | CC0 | <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Old_dry_cleaner%27s_storefront_(Unsplash).jpg> |
| `ozark-copper-letters.jpg` | Five three-dimensional copper letters spelling OZARK, laid on a table and shot at an angle. 963 by 341. | Public domain, United States National Park Service | <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Five_3-dimensional_copper_letters_that_spell_%22OZARK%22;_Ozark_Bathhouse_identification_sign;_letters_not_solid_but_molded;_each_(b58bc140-b4f0-45ce-8a6e-4fce37158f9d).jpg> |
| `handwriting-defg.jpg` | Four cursive handwritten letters, d e f g, on ruled lines that cross the strokes. 842 by 308. | Public domain | <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Handwriting_lineation.jpg> |

Why these three. The storefront is the easy real case: flat, sharp, high
contrast, with thirteen distinct capitals (A D E F G H I L N O R S T), so the
other thirteen have to be inferred. The copper letters are the hard real case:
perspective, depth, shadow and patina on only five letters. The handwriting is the
hard case of another kind: thin strokes, ruled lines running through the
letters, and no typeface behind them at all.
